title: The No-Start That Starts Fine for You (tree pilot)
complaintTemplate: CUST STATES: every week or so it cranks but won't fire — then twenty minutes later it starts like nothing happened. Always runs by the time it's towed in. Worse when it's hot out. No warning light stays on.

faultSeeds.internalNote: Crankshaft position sensor heat-soaks and drops out when hot, recovers when cool — the textbook intermittent. Only a capture during an actual failure shows it (no sync/RPM during crank). Bench tests and bay starts pass every time. Correct fix: crank sensor. Confirming test: the captured failure event.

activeFaults.label: crankshaft position sensor dropping out when heat-soaked

resultOverrides.act_capture: The logger catches it on day two — a hot no-start after a 20-minute shutdown. During crank the RPM/sync trace flatlines: no crankshaft-position signal reaching the ECM. Fuel pressure was normal beforehand, but spark and injector pulse never got the cue. It restarted once it cooled.
resultOverrides.act_freezeframe: One immature history code: P0335 (crankshaft position circuit). No freeze frame of a live fault.

faultSeeds.internalNote: Fuel pump intermittently fails to prime — no pressure during the event, but sync and spark are fine. Passes every bay start. Correct fix: fuel pump (or its relay/connector). Confirming test: the captured event showing 0 fuel pressure with sync/spark present.

activeFaults.label: fuel pump intermittently not priming (no pressure during the event)

resultOverrides.act_capture: The logger catches a no-start: during crank the RPM/sync is solid and spark is firing, but fuel pressure sits at 0 and the pump made no priming buzz at key-on. Next start, pressure was back.
resultOverrides.act_freezeframe: No stored codes — an intermittent pump dropout doesn't set one on this platform.

faultSeeds.internalNote: Intermittent immobilizer/anti-theft fault — the ECM isn't authorized to fuel during the event (no injector pulse, security light active), while sync/spark/fuel are all fine. The fix is a relearn / key or antenna-ring repair, NOT an engine part. Correct fix: immobilizer relearn. Confirming test: the captured event showing security active + no injector pulse.

activeFaults.label: intermittent immobilizer fault — ECM not authorized to fuel

resultOverrides.act_capture: The logger catches a no-start: sync present, spark present, fuel pressure normal — but zero injector pulse, and the security indicator was flashing through the event. The ECM isn't being authorized to fuel.
resultOverrides.act_freezeframe: No powertrain codes. An anti-theft / immobilizer event is logged, with no useful detail.

nodes.prompt: You try to start it — warm, cold, after a soak. It fires right up every time. It behaves for you exactly like it behaves for no one else; you won't catch this on your schedule in the bay.

options.label: Right — I can't chase what won't act up here. Back to the plan.

nodes.prompt: You wiggle harnesses, tap the crank sensor, and heat-gun the usual suspects. Nothing drops it on command — the fault refuses to perform for you.
nodes.continueLabel: It won't be provoked. Back to the plan.

nodes.prompt: Commit to a specific root cause — based on what a real failure event actually showed, not on what usually goes bad.

options.label: It's the crankshaft position sensor — replace it
It's the fuel pump — replace it (check relay and connector)
It's an immobilizer fault — key/antenna repair and relearn
Crank sensors always go on these — throw one at it
It always starts here — no fault found, return it

nodes.prompt: You replace the crankshaft position sensor, then heat-soak it and confirm the sync signal holds through a hot restart.
You replace the fuel pump (and check its relay and connector), then confirm prime and pressure across repeated hot key-ons.
nodes.continueLabel: Confirm prime and pressure, then release

nodes.prompt: You address the immobilizer fault — key/antenna-ring repair and a relearn — then confirm injector pulse returns and security clears across restarts.
You fixed what the failure event actually showed — confirmed across the exact conditions it used to die in. It stays started, and you can prove why.
It's towed back in a week — cranks, won't fire, then starts twenty minutes later. Nothing was ever captured, so nothing was actually diagnosed.
